name: TRPC1 - Ca2+ - PGC-1a - mitochondrial activation ("magnetic mitohormesis")
driver: unidentified; molecular requirement (TRPC1) and timing shown, physical driver not
driver_note: TRPC1 is necessary (CRISPR knockdown) and membrane-resident (Kurth 2020 vesicles). Aminoglycosides block. Sensitivity tracks TRPC1 expression and is lower after log phase. Field direction (up vs down) matters in quail embryos, but reversing a unipolar pulse flips both B and dB/dt sign, so direction does not separate B from dB/dt. Removing the ambient field lowered TRPC1 (a B effect with no dB/dt). The group's own review states rise time, dB/dt and symmetry are seldom disclosed.

f_Hz.note: frequency and waveform not in the primary abstracts

dBdt_Ts.basis: computed lower bound; pulse edges are probably faster

windows.schedule: 10 min single dose (cells); 10 min/week for 6 weeks to >4 months (mice); 5 x 10 min over 13 days (quail); apply near peak TRPC1 expression

evidence: in vitro and mouse, one lab lineage (NUS/Franco-Obregon); no independent replication retrieved
confidence: moderate that a TRPC1-dependent response exists in that lab's system; low on driver; low on translation
caveat: Yap 2019 full text returned empty, so waveform details are unverified. No amplitude series: minimum effective and ineffective B are not defined.

name: ROS generation and scavenging (SOD, catalase, antioxidant response)
driver: B (static fields are sufficient); time variation modifies but is not required
driver_note: Static fields (dB/dt = 0, E = 0) change ROS, mitochondrial Ca and MMP at 0.1-20 mT and also when the ambient field is removed (<5 uT). At equal peak B, static and 50 Hz fields differ in outcome (Alipour 2022 pHi and viability; Wang 2018 ATP), so dB/dt is a modifier. Direction is context dependent: ROS rises in unstressed cells, falls in pre-stressed cells (Merighi, Liao). No paper varied dB/dt at constant B for a therapy waveform.

dBdt_Ts.basis: computed; Sherrard assumes triangular rise over half of a 0.5 ms pulse; Merighi ~2 T/s from pick-up-coil inputs that could not be re-verified

E_Vm.basis: computed, 1 cm radius; all below the 0.1 V/m Weaver-Astumian broad-band limit

windows.nulls: Nieminen 2024: 100 and 500 uT, 50 Hz, no ROS change; Fei 2019: 0-4 mT pre-exposed medium no ROS; Goh 2025: 10-16 mT ROS unchanged and not required; Wang 2018: ATP changes uncorrelated with ROS/MMP

evidence: in vitro, several lineages; mostly abstract-level
confidence: moderate that 0.1-20 mT can change ROS under some conditions; low on sign and reproducibility; low on role of dB/dt
caveat: DCF dyes are non-specific. Sherrard's field-cancelling coil also removes dB/dt, so B and dB/dt are not separated even there. Bajtos 2025 (16.5 Hz, 10 uT window, 0.5 Hz or 250 nT reverses sign) is unreplicated and matches neither electron nor proton Larmor frequency.

name: Nrf2 / HO-1 antioxidant response
driver_note: Static 20 mT also raises Nrf2, so induction is not specific to time-varying fields. Shortest exposure tested 1 h at 1 mT (50 Hz); HO-1 peaks at 6 h.

windows.time_course: HO-1 mRNA and protein peak at 6 h; nuclear Nrf2 needs Akt and ERK

evidence: in vitro THP-1, MSC; mouse NAFLD (parameters not in abstract)

name: Mitochondrial respiration, membrane potential, ATP
driver: static B and orientation can shift bioenergetics; time variation modulates
driver_note: Inconsistent direction: respiration up at 1.5 mT (Yap, Tai); glycolytic shift at 4 mT/80 Hz (Liao); MMP preserved under insult (Merighi); hypomagnetic field lowers MMP and ATP, and acts directly on isolated mitochondria (Fu 2016); Usselman 2016 RF at Zeeman resonance, perpendicular vs parallel orientation gives ECAR +100 % vs OCR +54 %.

name: Radical-pair mechanism (flavin / superoxide, cryptochrome)
driver: B (instantaneous value and orientation); ELF frequency/dB/dt irrelevant because spin coherence is ns-us
driver_note: A 10-100 Hz field is quasi-static for a radical pair, so yield follows instantaneous B and the cycle average, not dB/dt. Frequency-selective effects need RF at the Larmor frequency (28.02 MHz/mT, 1.40 MHz at 50 uT) at 1-10 uT (Usselman, Castello, Gurhan 2023; Vacha 2009 onset 12-18 nT at 1.2 MHz). ELF resonance would need a near-zero bias (electron Larmor ~28 Hz at 1 nT) which a bipolar waveform crosses only briefly.

windows.B_threshold: sensitivity demonstrated at <=50 uT in model chemistry; ETF flavoenzyme 20 nT vs 50 uT gave H2O2 -13 %, O2.- +10 %

binhi_criterion.basis: computed with gamma 1.76e11 rad/s/T, kappa*tau neglected, tau 10-100 ns

windows.expected_magnitude: order 10 % shift in ROS product ratios, not a switch

evidence: chemistry and cell-free (strong); cells (single lineage); behavioural (cockroach)
confidence: low-moderate that RPM contributes at uT-mT; low that it explains PEMF therapy
caveat: Wang 2019 (human EEG) argues polarity sensitivity excludes an axial radical-pair compass. Hore 2012 PNAS and Adair 1991 abstracts not retrievable.

name: Biogenic magnetite torque / mechanosensitive channels (Piezo1, TRP)
driver: B (torque scales with B, not dB/dt)
driver_note: Computed m·B/kT for a single-domain magnetite cube (Ms 4.8e5 A/m): 30 nm 3.0, 50 nm 14, 80 nm 57 at 1 mT; 50 nm gives 0.7 at 50 uT. Kirschvink 1992 found >=5e6 crystals/g in human brain tissue. In the Kirschvink-Dobson model AC below ~10 Hz has minimal effect, pulsed or DC can force gates.

windows.B_mT: 0.5-5 mT gives 7-70 kT for a 50 nm crystal (computed)
windows.f_Hz: >~10 Hz per model; no PEMF-therapy measurement

evidence: theory plus magnetite measurement; no PEMF-specific Piezo1 data (search returned 0)
caveat: Meister 2016 shows ferritin-based magnetogenetics fails by 5-10 orders of magnitude. Engineered nanomagnet papers (Choi, Hao) do not show endogenous activation.

name: Diamagnetic anisotropy, Zeeman splitting and cyclotron resonance
driver_note: Orientation needs ~1 T (membranes), 8-14 T (cell alignment), 9 T (EGFR kinase), 16 T (Tau phase separation); orientation energy scales as B^2, so 5 mT carries 2.5e-5 of the 1 T value. mu_B·B/kT = 2.2e-6 at 1 mT. Ca2+ cyclotron: 0.766 Hz/uT, i.e. ~380-3800 Hz at 0.5-5 mT, not 10-100 Hz.
confidence: high that it is inapplicable at mT; low for the ICR report (single, unreplicated)

name: Weaver-Astumian limit applied to 0.5-5 mT, 10-100 Hz coils
driver_note: Cells can respond directly to ~0.1 V/m broad-band, or ~1e-4 V/m if narrow-band or signal-averaged. Macroscopic E for the coil range (culture well 1 cm, tissue loop 5 cm) is 0.16-79 mV/m: 1.3-3 orders below the broad-band limit and 1.6-790x above the narrow-band limit. A broad-band direct E detector is therefore excluded; a narrow-band or signal-averaging detector is not excluded at the 1.5 mT/50 Hz and 5 mT/100 Hz end.

E_Vm.basis: computed, uniform B, circular path; the r = 10 um single-cell column is NOT what a cell experiences

confidence: high for the physics; no narrow-band detector has been demonstrated
caveat: Adair 1991 abstract unavailable, numbers not quoted.
